column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls both groups sons, of humankind and of a man; BSB interprets them as low and high.
The Hebrew has plural wisdoms and understandings; BSB has singular wisdom and understanding.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the iniquity of his heels; BSB describes wicked usurpers surrounding him.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has their soul with a plural possessor and speaks of ceasing forever; BSB has his soul and describes payment never sufficing.
The Hebrew names the pit; BSB says decay.
The Hebrew says he sees that wise people die; BSB says it is clear.
The Hebrew wording begins with their inner thought or being, not graves; BSB begins with their graves as eternal homes.
The Hebrew names honor and not remaining overnight; BSB names wealth and not enduring.
The Hebrew names their way and folly and their mouth; BSB describes the fate of self-confident people and endorsing sayings.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names Sheol’s hand and taking him without an explicit to Himself; BSB omits hand and adds to Himself.
The Hebrew says do not fear; BSB says do not be amazed.
The Hebrew names his honor; BSB says abundance.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not separately name day after light; BSB adds of day.
The Hebrew names honor; BSB says riches.
